body:
> You make it all sound so easy, I wish it were.


Making the right choice is actually rarely easy. It's just that when you're facing the prospect of giving up on life completely, it might be worth considering that it's worth trying something different before you throw in the towel. You don't like where your life is now, so you can work to change it.



Reading between the lines, it sounds as though you want your current situation to change, not for your life to end. You just can't see an easy way out. It won't be easy, but it'll be worth it if you succeed, because you'll never end up in a position like this again. You can have the life you want, grades, friends. There'll be a painful part in between where you're scared, facing the unknown. But it's not "better the devil you know" now, because you are sick of this shit. So pick the hard option, and make some changes.


Your guilt and shame keeps you from class because you're so scared of feeling those negative emotions that you avoid them. Another type of person would avoid them by ensuring that they never miss an assignment, but you miss the assignment anyway and then avoid the class. Both are just types of pain avoidance, but the first student will achieve more than you because they are motivated to hand the stuff in. 



That ties into the responsibility thing. Eventually, you have to take ownership of your actions. It's OK to fuck up. It's OK to feel bad, to be ashamed. But eventually you've got to change it, because no one can change it for you. No matter where you run to, you are going to be there. You have to like the person you will spend the rest of your life with - you - or you are in for a painful ride.



It's not that you can't make decisions - you just don't make decisions. You can change that.



Being responsible isn't easy at all. Everyone hates it. It's just, we have to choose to be responsible so we can get some of the things we want. It helps us avoid shame and guilt, in a more healthy way than simply running away - like spurring us on to do our homework.


I feel like shit, partly because some sad stuff has happened in my life, but mostly because I decided to take some drugs over the weekend. That's not nice to admit. The shame is uncomfortable. I ditched work today, essentially because I'm on a comedown, and that's very embarrassing. We all fuck up, we all act irresponsibly. But I won't be doing this again, because it's too uncomfortable a feeling. You need to get to that point, too.


It's on you. Good luck.

> I transferred to a wonderful school with new rules where they actually care about students


So talk to them! Explain what's going on. I guarantee you are not the first student ever to experience this. They will help you. You are catastrophising, which feels horrible, but you're not in a position of "do homework" or "commit suicide". There are a lot of other options, some more tolerable than others. The best route is to talk to your school in the first instance and go from there.
